title: The Pelican dance hall on Rampart and Gravier
summary: Dejan explains that 'the Pelican' was a dance place on Rampart, with an annex where visiting bandsmen jammed all night; he also recalls schoolmates and boyhood.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You said, what was the Pelican? You mean that?
That was on the corner of the...
Oh, you mean that place up on Rampart, yeah.
Yeah, on the corner of Rampart and Grab, yeah.
It sounded like you said on the Pelican like it was a boat or something.

Well, it was on the Pelican. Was it a roof? No, it was not a roof. It was just a dance office where we'd go. We said, we're going on the Pelican tonight, you know. Yeah. And the next block was Astoria. Yeah, I remember that.

Well, at the Pelican, when I had the Pelican, when I had the Pelican, the Pelican annex on the bottom, you see. And when the fellas come in at night off the boat and bands come in town, well, that's where they used to go jam all night long.
I won't say dinner there. They must not have had segregation those days. What? That's when Bunk Johnson first came to town. Well, I tell you now, a long time ago,

things were mighty nice around town. That was 1942. I always did go hours ago. I mean, because I know how to care of myself and take care of myself. But I mean, people didn't go all foolish like that. People are foolish, you know. We used to have some boys across the street at my house. The boys would start playing saxophone. My brother and I was playing music and live across the street at my house. We used to go to school together every morning. We used to stand, just carve a school around on the Man Street. Well, it was Willa McG Rogers, I think. And we used to stand in front of the school and wait until we come and buy them to school and even walk home together. Yeah, they never had a lot of, I mean, it's just, it's something, I don't know, something went haywire. When did you first go on the boat, sir?
